notes: Ambiguities and friction in following the skill. (1) The paper text is a short workshop paper (footer 'ICML 2025 Workshop') but the user asked for ICLR; the skill has no workshop-vs-main-track guidance, so I judged it against the ICLR pool as instructed. (2) The extracted text lists author names although the file is called blinded.txt; I used them only in the literature-check fingerprint for exclusion and ignored them for scoring. (3) related_search.py counts hyphenated words (e.g. 'arbitrary-scale') as two concept words, so queries are refused at 5 words; refusals are not counted against the budget. (4) Phase 1.6 report check is described as running after the reports are drafted but the skill does not say whether the written reports should show the pre-check or post-check text; I presented post-check text plus a change table. (5) The skill says to mark a prior work's novelty from its abstract only, yet the script stores truncated abstracts (about 500 chars), so claims about what a prior work does rest partly on titles and knowledge; I marked uncertain items [verify]. (6) The 'before' run uses default eic_weight 1.0 when the field is omitted; the DA-critical list was empty in both runs. (7) The ICLR rating label is printed on two scales ({0,2,4,6,8,10} and {1,3,5,6,8,10}); I report both. (8) I used a PSNR-vs-MSE identity check (constant peak per table) to find a Table 3 inconsistency; the skill's error audit supports recomputation but does not mention metric-identity checks. (9) Text-extraction interleaves the two columns, so verbatim quotes spanning line breaks could not be matched by plain text search; evidence.json uses short quotes that match the normalized text. (10) An extra file aggregate_preview.md and helper files (fingerprint.json, novelty_profile.json, reviewer_copy.txt, kept results ledgers) exist in the results directory as by-products.
